scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Chief Financial Officer,

Your two stated measures pull in different directions over the next six months, and it is worth being direct about that. The DOT compliance audit opens in six months; a two-year, $4,200,000 migration will not be finished by then, and no part of moving load-matching and carrier-settlement workloads to Google Cloud should be presented to auditors as a remediation. What the programme does offer for the audit window is evidentiary: consolidating 28 SQL Server instances and 620 Hyper-V virtual machines onto Google Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL forces a complete inventory of where settlement records live, who touches them, and how long they are retained — the three questions that most often turn a routine audit into a finding. We recommend sequencing a discovery and data-lineage workstream in the first 90 days, funded inside the programme, so the audit is supported by documented controls rather than by the migration itself. Your compliance posture in six months will rest on that inventory work and on your existing on-premises controls, both of which we will help you evidence.

On the $1,850,000 annual technology spend, expect the programme to raise your run-rate before it lowers it. During migration you will carry both estates, and the licence position changes materially: moving off SQL Server to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL retires per-core SQL Server licensing and Hyper-V host costs, but incurs re-platforming effort on stored procedures and settlement batch logic, which is the single largest cost and schedule risk in the plan. Realistic shape: elevated spend through roughly the first 12–15 months, crossover late in year two, with steady-state savings driven mainly by licence retirement and by right-sizing 620 VMs that were provisioned for peak. We are not asking you to accept that as a promise — we propose a fixed-scope discovery phase that produces a validated baseline of the current $1,850,000, a bottom-up target-state run-rate, and a dated crossover point, so you can hold the programme to a number you have seen derived rather than one we asserted. If that analysis does not show a defensible return, the right decision is to stop after discovery, and the contract should let you do so.
